primitives.name: Hazard Bearing Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is not physically necessary that they be permanently hazarded by the owners, that the actual producers should get their entire wage in advance of the completion of the process, but this is the way it works out under free contract.
primitives.assumptions: Producers bear risk proportional to time-to-completion; wages paid ex-ante under free contract.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When risk is not borne by owners, systemic instability emerges due to misaligned incentives.

Hazard bearing and ownership permutation define a dualism where risk is neither deterministic nor uniformly distributed. In GSI, this manifests as a Bayesian belief update over risk parameters, where each agent's wage payment schedule reflects posterior beliefs about project success. The GSE interprets this through a Markovian lens, modeling transitions between states of ownership and risk exposure. The failure mode arises when the assumption of rational hazard bearing breaks down—either through asymmetric information or moral hazard. This duality creates a bifurcation in social organization: either agents internalize risk (free contract), or society externalizes it (collective ownership). The mathematical formalism captures this as a partition function over risk states, with entropy encoding the degree of social coordination. The epistemic trace reveals that while the system appears to evolve naturally under free contract, it is actually constrained by the axioms of individual rationality and bounded information processing.
